questions.q: Why does Percona XtraBackup exist, per this lesson?
options: MySQL ships no built-in equivalent to RMAN or BACKUP DATABASE for fast, hot, physical backups of InnoDB at scale
XtraBackup is required to install MySQL
mysqldump was discontinued and needed a replacement
MySQL cannot run without XtraBackup installed
questions.explain: Unlike Oracle's RMAN or SQL Server's native backup tooling, MySQL has no built-in hot physical backup utility, which XtraBackup fills.

questions.q: What does the xtrabackup --backup step actually do, per this lesson?
options: Runs a full mysqldump export in the background
Deletes the existing data files before copying new ones
Copies InnoDB's data files while streaming redo log changes generated during the copy
Permanently locks all tables until the backup finishes
questions.explain: The --backup step copies files while capturing redo log entries, without needing to stop the server or block writers for most of its runtime.

questions.q: Why is the xtrabackup --prepare step necessary before restoring, per this lesson?
options: It replays the captured redo log against the copied files to bring them to a consistent, restorable state
It uploads the backup to Percona's servers
It compresses the backup files to save disk space
It converts the backup into a mysqldump-compatible SQL file
questions.explain: Without --prepare, the copied files aren't yet consistent — --prepare applies the same crash-recovery logic InnoDB uses after an unclean shutdown.

questions.q: How does an XtraBackup restore work, per this lesson?
options: Stop MySQL, copy the prepared files into the data directory with --copy-back, then start the server
XtraBackup backups cannot be restored, only inspected
Run RESTORE DATABASE against the XtraBackup files
Replay the SQL file with the mysql client, same as mysqldump
questions.explain: Because it's a physical backup, restoring means placing prepared files back into MySQL's data directory and starting the server — no SQL replay.

questions.q: Why is XtraBackup considered the industry-standard choice for large MySQL databases, per this lesson?
options: It's free, open-source, and large-scale MySQL shops actually run it in production because mysqldump doesn't scale to their restore-time requirements
It replaces the need for any backup strategy at all
It is slower than mysqldump but more secure
It is the only backup tool MySQL's license permits
questions.explain: XtraBackup is framed as the honest, real-world standard tool for large databases, filling a genuine gap rather than being an arbitrary add-on.
